# Firmware

## Overview

The firmware for the Aurora Labs Nova Widget v2 and related sensor products manages device operations, sensor reading intervals, and self-healing mesh networking via MeshSync. Firmware version iterations (such as 0.3.8 and 0.9.3) target optimization of power consumption, pairing reliability, and sensor polling frequencies.

## Key Details

- **Reading Interval:** The default reading interval is set to **15 minutes** when the mesh is active (configured in firmware version 0.3.8), though it is user-configurable from 5 minutes to 24 hours via the companion app. 
- **MeshSync Protocol:** Devices utilize a self-healing mesh with a maximum hop count of 4, connecting to a gateway node (USB-powered) that bridges to MQTT. 
- **Power and Battery Targets:** Target average current is kept under 85 µA, including mesh overhead in a 10-node deployment. Beta testing feedback indicated pairing complaints decreased following firmware version 0.9.3.
- **OTA Updates:** Over-the-air (OTA) updates are currently deferred to firmware version v2.1.

## Related Entities

- **Aurora Labs:** The manufacturer of the Nova Widget v2 and sensor systems.
- **Mira Chen:** Author of the product spec draft and field reports detailing battery drain issues.
- **Jonah Park:** Engineering team member tracking meshsync pairing stability.
- **Alex Kim & Jamie QA:** Product and QA team members tracking documentation alignment and beta NPS metrics.

## Related Concepts

- **MeshSync:** The proprietary mesh networking protocol responsible for device-to-device relay and MQTT gateway bridging.
- **Battery Drain & Relay Mode:** Field reports indicate that enabling MeshSync relay mode can increase battery drain if the relay radio fails to sleep between hops (tracked as MESH-118).
- **Enclosure and Hardware Integration:** Firmware interacts closely with hardware components including the Nordic nRF52840 MCU, SHT41 temp/humidity sensor, VEML7700 light sensor, and capacitive soil probe, housed within IP54-rated enclosures.

## Contradictions

> **Contradiction:** Internal product documentation and marketing materials conflict regarding the default reading interval. While the product spec draft and firmware defaults establish a 15-minute interval, herbal box copy and marketing PDFs have alternatively referenced a 5-minute interval, and kickoff notes previously mentioned an hourly default.
